newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-MARSH PUTS TASMANIA IN STRONG POSITION.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MARSH PUTS TASMANIA IN STRONG POSITION.

text.p: Tasmania all-rounder Daniel Marsh produced his most profitable day in first-class cricket on Friday to put his side in a strong position in their Sheffield Shield match against Victoria.
Marsh, the son of former Australia wicket-keeper Rod Marsh, was denied his maiden century but hit a career-high score of 97 as Tasmania reached 359 for seven declared in their first innings.
The 23-year-old fell leg before wicket to pace bowler David Saker three runs short of a century but his innings allowed Tasmania to build substantially on their overnight score of 250 for six.
Marsh, who bowls off-spin, then took the wickets of opener Graeme Vimpani for 62 and all-rounder Ian Harvey for two as Victoria crumbled to be 174 for six in reply at stumps on the second day.
In Sydney, New South Wales led by the slender margin of 65 runs on the second day of their match against Western Australia after reaching 183 for four in the second innings.

New South Wales, dismissed for a paltry 126 in the first innings on Thursday, allowed Western Australia to add 64 runs to their overnight score of 180 for eight before the visitors were dismissed for 244.
Opener Rodney Davison got New South Wales off to a better start in their second innings and was 79 not out at the close.
Western Australia and New South Wales are battling for second place in the Shield standings behind leaders Queensland.

In Adelaide, middle-order batsman Darren Lehmann scored more than half of his side's runs as South Australia reached 323 for five at stumps on the first day of their match against the unbeaten Queensland.
Lehmann was 165 not out after century partnerships with captain Jamie Siddons and wicket-keeper Tim Nielsen. Siddons made 61 and Nielsen was 28 not out.
